title: 日本のお正月
summary: The article describes how Japanese people celebrate New Year by resting with family, eating mochi and ozoni, and visiting a shrine to pray for health and good fortune.

title: 山で紅葉を見ます
titleTranslation: Seeing Autumn Leaves in the Mountains
summary: The writer describes hiking in the mountains on weekends during autumn to enjoy the changing colors of the leaves with friends.

title: 朝の駅
summary: The article describes how a train station becomes busy and crowded every morning as many people rush to catch trains to work and school.

title: 私の小さい部屋
summary: The narrator describes their small but beloved room, filled with cherished items including a plant they water daily and an old chair that belonged to their grandmother.

title: 友だちとカラオケ
summary: The narrator describes going to karaoke with friends on Saturday, taking turns singing, enjoying drinks and snacks, and feeling refreshed and stress-free afterward.

title: 日本の自動販売機
summary: This article explains that vending machines are found everywhere in Japan and describes how to buy hot or cold drinks from them.

title: お弁当
summary: The article explains how Japanese people prepare or buy bento boxed lunches and why bento are an important part of daily life in Japan.

title: 風邪をひきました
summary: The narrator describes catching a cold, visiting the doctor, taking medicine, and resting in hopes of recovering quickly.

title: 家でカレーライスを作ります
summary: The article explains how to make Japan's popular curry rice at home by cutting and cooking vegetables and meat, then serving it with hot rice.

title: 図書館の静かな一日
titleTranslation: A Quiet Day at the Library
summary: The narrator spends a peaceful day reading quietly in the library by a window, enjoying the sunny weather and birdsong while only drinking water since beverages aren't allowed inside.

title: わたしのしゅみ:スマホで写真をとること
titleTranslation: My Hobby: Taking Photos with My Smartphone
summary: The author's hobby is taking photos with a smartphone, enjoying pictures of the sky and flowers, and feeling happy when friends admire the photos they share.

title: 冬の日本
summary: The article describes how Japanese winters are cold and snowy, with children playing in the snow and people warming up indoors with kotatsu and hot drinks.

title: ゆうびんきょくで てがみを だします
titleTranslation: Sending a Letter at the Post Office
summary: The narrator visits the post office to buy a stamp, mail a letter to a friend, and enjoys the experience of handwriting despite having to wait a little.

title: 週末の部屋そうじ
summary: A person describes their weekend routine of cleaning their room, from opening the windows to vacuuming and finally taking a shower.

title: カフェで コーヒーと ケーキ
titleTranslation: At the Cafe: Coffee and Cake
summary: A person visits a small cafe on a hot day, orders coffee and cake, and enjoys a quiet moment looking out the window.

title: 夏祭り
summary: The article describes a fun summer festival with food stalls, yukata, shaved ice, and fireworks at night.

title: おふろと おんせん
summary: The narrator explains why they love baths and describes how Japanese hot springs (onsen) work, ending with a wish to visit one this weekend.

title: わたしの かぞく
summary: The narrator introduces their family of four—father, mother, older brother, and themselves—describing each person's job or studies and their daily life together.

title: 雨と傘
summary: The article describes Japan's rainy season around June, when people use umbrellas and rain boots to stay dry as the streets get wet.

title: スーパーで買い物
summary: A person visits the supermarket near their house to buy vegetables, fruit, bread, and milk for 500 yen total, and looks forward to going again tomorrow.

title: ラーメンの店
summary: The writer loves ramen and describes visiting a ramen shop, what's in the dish, and enjoying the meal with chopsticks.

title: 日本の四季
summary: The article introduces Japan's four seasons and describes the characteristic weather and activities of each one.

title: こうえんへ いきます
summary: The narrator visits a park on a nice day and enjoys the trees, flowers, birds, playing children and dogs, and a quiet moment on a bench before promising to return.

title: 日本と猫
summary: The article introduces Japan's love of cats, including popular cat cafes and the lucky beckoning cat figurine called maneki-neko.

title: すし
summary: An introduction to sushi as a popular Japanese food made with rice and fish, eaten in various styles with hands or chopsticks and dipped in soy sauce.

title: 桜と花見
summary: The article explains hanami, the Japanese tradition of viewing cherry blossoms in parks with friends and family.

title: 日本の電車
summary: This article describes how convenient, fast, and reliable trains are in Japan, covering IC card use at ticket gates and the quiet etiquette passengers follow.

title: 朝ごはん
summary: The article explains that Japanese breakfast typically includes rice, miso soup, and sometimes strong-smelling but healthy natto, and describes it as simple and delicious.

title: コンビニ
summary: The article describes how convenient stores are, being open all hours and selling a wide variety of items like food, drinks, magazines, and tickets.

title: わたしの一日
summary: The narrator describes their daily routine from waking up in the morning to going to bed at night.

title: 駅弁の楽しみ
titleTranslation: The Joy of Ekiben (Station Lunch Boxes)
summary: The article explains what ekiben (station lunch boxes) are, their long history, regional variety, and the enjoyment of choosing and eating them while traveling by train in Japan.

title: 銭湯に行ってみましょう
titleTranslation: Let's Go to a Sento (Public Bath)
summary: The article introduces Japanese public bathhouses called sento, covering their history, bathing rules, features, and the social role they play for local communities.

title: コンビニのおにぎり
summary: The article explains what onigiri (Japanese rice balls) are, how they are eaten, and why they are popular and convenient in Japanese daily life.

title: 日本の「はんこ」
summary: The article explains what a hanko (personal name stamp) is, how and when Japanese people use it in daily life, and how it is gradually being supplemented by signatures.

title: 日本の自動販売機
summary: This article explains that Japan has an unusually large number of vending machines, which are conveniently available everywhere and at all hours, offering both hot and cold drinks with cash or electronic payment.

title: 折り紙のはなし
summary: This article introduces origami, Japan's traditional paper-folding play, explaining how it is done, its most famous form (the crane), and its popularity both in Japan and abroad.
